positive.title: direct-only local def reads an outer parameter
assertions: add is proven closed by direct local calls only
base is read live at call time
no capture environment is acquired

positive.title: immediately invoked closure reads an outer let
assertions: immediate invocation is an exact closed proof route
the immutable ancestor place is read-only

positive.title: direct local calls observe the current outer var value
assertions: the callable only reads the outer var
the result observes value 2 rather than a creation-time snapshot

positive.title: exact selected scoped formal admits call-duration lexical access
assertions: the exact selected formal is scoped
the lexical dependency is bounded by the call

positive.title: pure callable reads immutable inert data
assertions: base is immutable
the dependency introduces no authority, resource, shared state, or effect

positive.title: effectful local def may still use qualified lexical access
assertions: lexical access does not imply purity
the declared io effect remains on the callable profile

positive.title: nested callable may read an ancestor closure field and frame parameter
assertions: the outer closure explicitly owns seed
the nested direct-only def has lexical dependencies on seed and delta
explicit environment and region binding are orthogonal

positive.title: explicit copy retains snapshot semantics
assertions: the explicit copy is acquired at closure creation
the result observes the snapshot value 1

positive.title: empty capture list permits module dependencies
assertions: the callable has no ancestor-frame dependency
empty capture syntax is not a purity or dependency-free assertion

positive.title: bare capture item preserves current compatibility
assertions: base remains a current bare capture item
the syntax is not reinterpreted as inferred lexical access

negative.title: returning a lexical callable escapes
assertions: return is an escape sink
no exact closed proof exists

negative.title: ordinary callable argument is not a scoped proof
negative.source:
def consume(f: () -> Int) -> Int = { return f() }
def bad(base: Int) -> Int = { return consume({ => base }) }
assertions: an ordinary formal may store or return the callable
the selected formal is not exact #scoped

negative.title: storing a lexical callable in a field escapes
assertions: field storage is an escape sink

negative.title: lexical access cannot write an outer place
assertions: qualified lexical access is read-only

negative.title: lexical access cannot move an outer owner
assertions: moving an ancestor owner requires an explicit ownership mechanism

negative.title: async local def is excluded
assertions: suspension can outlive the ancestor activation

negative.title: generator owner is excluded
assertions: a generator may suspend beyond the ancestor activation

negative.title: spawn is an escape and concurrency sink
assertions: spawn crosses both activation and concurrency boundaries

negative.title: actor transfer is excluded
assertions: actor transfer crosses isolation

negative.title: empty capture assertion rejects an ancestor dependency
assertions: present-empty and absent capture syntax are semantically distinct

negative.title: lexical read after outer move is invalid
assertions: the ancestor place must be live at each call

negative.title: pure lexical callable cannot read mutable shared state
assertions: pure admission excludes mutable shared state

negative.title: guard-owned lexical dependency is excluded
assertions: guard owners are outside the R1 admission domain

negative.title: borrow rooted in an ancestor cannot outlive the call
assertions: the derived borrow escapes its call-duration requirement

negative.title: explicit capture does not make a residual lexical escape safe
assertions: seed is environment-owned
offset remains region-bound
the residual lexical dependency prevents escape

boundary.title: absent capture syntax differs from present-empty syntax
boundary.accepted_source: def demo(base: Int) -> Int = { return { => base }() }
boundary.rejected_source: def demo(base: Int) -> Int = { return [] { => base }() }
assertions: absence permits inference
empty brackets assert an empty ancestor dependency set

boundary.title: live lexical read differs from explicit copy snapshot
boundary.accepted_source: var n = 1; def read() -> Int = { return n }; n = 2; assert read() == 2
boundary.rejected_source: var n = 1; let read = [copy n] { => n }; n = 2; assert read() == 2
assertions: lexical access reads at call time
copy capture reads its creation-time snapshot

boundary.title: exact scoped formal differs from ordinary formal
boundary.accepted_source: useNow({ => base }) where useNow: (#scoped () -> Int) -> Int
boundary.rejected_source: consume({ => base }) where consume: (() -> Int) -> Int
assertions: only the exact selected scoped formal supplies the proof

boundary.title: bare explicit capture differs from an empty closed assertion
assertions: the source remains accepted with its current capture-item meaning
empty brackets instead assert zero ancestor-frame dependencies

boundary.title: mixed explicit capture and lexical dependency remains region-bound
boundary.accepted_source: let f = [copy seed] { => seed + offset }; return f()
boundary.rejected_source: let f = [copy seed] { => seed + offset }; return f
assertions: environment state and residence state are separate axes

boundary.title: empty capture assertion permits module but not ancestor dependency
assertions: empty brackets are not a global dependency-free assertion

boundary.title: direct calls differ from alias or aggregate flow
boundary.accepted_source: def read() -> Int = { return base }; return read()
boundary.rejected_source: def read() -> Int = { return base }; let table = [read]; return table[0]()
assertions: the direct-call proof is syntactic and flow-bounded
aggregate storage invalidates that proof route

boundary.title: known proof differs from opaque flow
boundary.accepted_source: withNow({ => base }) where the exact selected formal is #scoped
boundary.rejected_source: opaqueHigherOrder({ => base }) where callable flow is unknown
assertions: unknown proof rejects

mutation.title: outer value mutation changes a later live read
mutation.base_source: var n = 1; def read() -> Int = { return n }; return read()
mutation.mutated_source: var n = 1; def read() -> Int = { return n }; n = 2; return read()
mutation.invariant: Both programs are admitted; the observable result changes from 1 to 2 because lexical reads are live.

mutation.title: adding explicit copy changes live access to snapshot
mutation.base_source: var n = 1; let read = { => n }; n = 2; return read()
mutation.mutated_source: var n = 1; let read = [copy n] { => n }; n = 2; return read()
mutation.invariant: Both programs are admitted; the observable result changes from live value 2 to snapshot value 1.

mutation.title: returning a direct-only local callable destroys the closed proof
mutation.base_source: def read() -> Int = { return base }; return read()
mutation.mutated_source: def read() -> Int = { return base }; return read
mutation.invariant: Changing invocation to callable return introduces an escape sink.

mutation.title: changing a scoped formal to ordinary destroys the proof
mutation.base_source: useNow({ => base }) where useNow: (#scoped () -> Int) -> Int
mutation.mutated_source: useNow({ => base }) where useNow: (() -> Int) -> Int
mutation.invariant: Only an exact selected scoped formal supplies call-duration closure.

mutation.title: changing an ancestor read to a move is rejected
mutation.invariant: Qualified lexical access is read-only and nonconsuming.
